idea-plugin.name: cem
idea-plugin.description:
Run the cem CLI from inside PyCharm / IntelliJ IDEA / GoLand / WebStorm / RubyMine / PhpStorm / Rider / CLion.

One AI thinks, another writes the code. Use a strong model for the reasoning and a cheap one for the typing: in pair mode the thinker is told not to write code — it produces a short plan (file, signature, approach, edge cases) and hands it to the writer, so the same work is not billed twice.

How to use it

  1. Select some code in the editor. No selection = the cursor lands in the input box at the bottom of the cem tool window.
  2. Press a shortcut, or use Tools → cem / the editor context menu.
  3. Read the result in the cem tool window at the bottom — each run gets its own tab.
Ctrl+Alt+Ithink ask the thinker about the selection
Ctrl+Alt+Wwrite have the writer implement it
Ctrl+Alt+Ppair thinker plans, writer codes

Examples

  • Select a function → Ctrl+Alt+P → "add retries with exponential backoff"
  • Select a failing test → Ctrl+Alt+I → "why does this fail?" — reasoning only, nothing is written
  • No selection → Ctrl+Alt+W → the input box opens in write mode, ready to type; to send a whole file, right-click it in the project tree (cem: review file… / ask about file…)
  • Interactive tab: type a prompt and press Enter, like a REPL. The selector on the left picks the mode (pair / think / write), Shift+Enter adds a line and ↑/↓ walk through earlier prompts

The working directory is the project root, so a project-level .cem.yaml (roles, models, reasoning effort) applies exactly as it does in the terminal.

Setup

Install the cem CLI first: curl -fsSL cem.pw/install | sh (PowerShell: irm cem.pw/install | iex). If the IDE cannot find it on PATH, set an absolute path in Settings → Tools → cem.

Automatic updates: add this once under Settings → Plugins → ⚙ → Manage Plugin Repositories:
https://github.com/muslu/cem/releases/latest/download/updatePlugins.xml
